claimText: Jingle Bells (opening refrain, arranged for beginners): the modern chorus in C major, values doubled, with our own bass

checks.source: https://archive.org/details/mostpopularhomes00nobl (The most popular home songs, New York: Hinds, Hayden & Eldredge, 1913; "Jingle, Bells", arr. George Rosey, copyright 1908, pp. 54-55)
checks.result: The modern chorus ("Jingle, bells! jingle, bells!"), G major, 4/4 with eighths. With every value doubled and transposed to C, the item matches its last four bars in pitch and order, except one note.
differences: bars 5-6: "to ride in a" - the printing has two sixteenths B-B on "in a" (E-E in C); the item has one E
bars 3 and 5: the dotted figure on "Jingle all" and the dotted and sixteenth notes of "Oh! what fun" are even quarters
bars 4 and 8: the last note is held for the whole bar

outcomeNote: Checked by eye 2026-09-24 against a 1908 public-domain printing with the modern chorus (research R11 table B). Pitches and order match, transposed from G to C with values doubled, except that "in a" is sung on one note; the rhythm is made plain. All named in departures. No note changed.
